observations.title: Kilauea volcano (United States)
observations.description: The Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO) reported that the eruption within Kilauea?s Kaluapele summit caldera, characterized by incandescence, intermittent spatter, and lava flows from craters and vents along the SW and W margins of Halema`uma`u Crater, continued at variable levels during 16-23 September. During 14-16 September five new vents opened N of the older vent complex (with N, W, and S vents), on and near the NW wall of Halema`uma`u Crater, and produced small lava flows. Intermittent bursts of spatter continued to build a small cone around the N vent, which reached 11-12 m tall by 14 September, and sporadic spatter bursts were also observed from the S and W vents. At around 1700 on 16 September a sixth vent opened to the N of the previous vent cluster; activity at all six vents stopped by 2030. Spattering at the older N, W, and S vents stopped during 1900-2100. Occasional incandescence and flames were observed in webcams images from the N, W, and S vents during 17-23 September, and minor intermittent spatter was variable at all three vents during 20-22 September. A very small, spatter-fed lava flow traveled 5-10 m from the N vent cone between 1923-1924 on 21 September. Lava vigorously overflowed the N vent during about 2210-2234 on 22 September, followed by another overflow at 2344. The Volcano Alert Level remained at Watch (the second highest level on a four-level scale) and the Aviation Color Code at Orange (the second highest color on a four-color scale). Source: US Geological Survey Hawaiian Volcano Observatory (HVO)
